head: Not this

rows: wa maa adraaka: 2 counts because the hamza is in another word
wa maaaa adraaka: 4 or 5 counts, as in our muttasil

keywords.def: lengthening a vowel sound, counted in beats (harakat)
separated madd: hamza in the next word
joined madd: hamza in the same word

questions.q: Read 74:24 to 27 and classify every madd before a hamza.
questions.a: هَٰذَآ إِلَّا (74:24) munfasil; هَٰذَآ إِلَّا (74:25) munfasil; وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ (74:27) munfasil.

questions.q: Rubric recitation: recite 74:11 to 30 to a partner in breakout rooms; partner scores the 'rules' row for madd only (pupil PDF). Today's rota group recites to the teacher.
questions.a: Partner records each munfasil and muttasil and whether lengths matched.

questions.q: Extend: find two munfasil in Al-Mulk.
questions.a: Pupil gives two examples with ayah numbers, checked by the teacher.

questions.q: Stretch: explain why muttasil must not be shorter than munfasil.
questions.a: Muttasil is the stronger (obligatory) madd, so it is never given less length than the optional one.
A) Munfasil. The alif ends كَلَّآ and the hamza begins إِنَّهُۥ: separated.

questions.q: Think again: One madd joins inside a word; another waits until the next word. Should they be treated the same?
questions.a: Muttasil is in one word and obligatory; munfasil is across two words; in our route both are 4 or 5, kept consistent.
